1

Introduction and problem statement

Purpose

How to read the notation

Symbols follow full quantity names: power (P), torque (M), rotational speed (n), vehicle speed (v), mass (m), force (F), energy (E), voltage (U), current (I), resistance (R), and efficiency (η). Lowercase p denotes pressure. A subscript identifies the component or operating mode, for example, PS1 — continuous power, Mpeak — peak torque.

An internal combustion engine (ICE) may use spark ignition (SI) or compression ignition (CI). PFI means port fuel injection; DI means direct injection, and GDI means gasoline direct injection. The slider-crank mechanism and valve gear are distinguished; TDC and BDC mean top and bottom dead centre, and CA means crank angle.

BEV means battery electric vehicle; HEV means hybrid electric vehicle; PHEV means plug-in hybrid electric vehicle. P2 is a parallel layout with an electric machine between the engine and gearbox. The battery's SOC is its state of charge; OCV is open-circuit voltage ( Uoc). Equivalent battery internal resistance is Rint; this is an ohmic internal-resistance model. NMC means lithium-ion nickel manganese cobalt oxide; LFP means lithium iron phosphate, LiFePO₄. Chemistry alone does not determine pack voltage, specific energy, or current limits.

PMSM means permanent-magnet synchronous motor. d and q are the direct and quadrature axes of a rotating coordinate system; Ld and Lq — axis inductances; ψ is flux linkage. RMS means root mean square; for a sinusoid, peak amplitude equals √2 times RMS. In phase voltage, peak denotes amplitude; in power/torque characteristics, it denotes short-duration duty. DC means direct current; AC means alternating current. S1 is continuous duty under steady thermal conditions; peak is short-duration peak duty. SVPWM means space-vector pulse-width modulation.

WLTP means Worldwide harmonized Light vehicles Test Procedure; its driving cycle is WLTC, Worldwide harmonized Light vehicles Test Cycle. PER means pure electric range. UBE means usable battery energy, measured here at the terminals; energy consumption per distance is (ECDC). CSS means constant-speed segment; M and E denote intermediate and final segments. The index in WLTC1, WLTC2 denotes the repetition number, not another cycle class.

EPA is the US Environmental Protection Agency. ALPHA means Advanced Light-duty Powertrain and Hybrid Analysis. UDDS is the Urban Dynamometer Driving Schedule; HWFET is the Highway Fuel Economy Test; US06 is the aggressive supplementary schedule. These names identify specific speed profiles.

ECU means electronic control unit; BMS means battery management system; OBD2 means second-generation on-board diagnostics. RMSE means root mean square error. The International System of Units (SI) is distinguished by context from SI meaning spark ignition. File formats are PDF (Portable Document Format), CSV (Comma-Separated Values), JSON (JavaScript Object Notation), SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics), HTML (HyperText Markup Language); ZIP is an archive format.

This is a general design and verification calculation for an engine and powertrain. First specify the required performance and adopt the parameters, then check the processes, dimensions, and subsequent calculations.

Selecting a petrol engine, diesel engine, hybrid, or BEV changes the active fields and chapters. The carburettor branch is excluded. Modern injection and boosting are represented by the available model; Euro 5–6 emissions compliance is not numerically verified.

Preq is a requirement; Pcalc is a result. Calculated and adopted geometry are stored separately. Changing the inputs makes all dependent results stale until recalculation.

Calculation assumptions and initial dimensions

Internal combustion engine calculation

The elemental C/H/O composition and oxygen mass fraction in air of 0.23 determine theoretical air demand. The effective heat capacities cv(T)=675+0.25T and R=287 are not chemical-equilibrium properties of the products.

In design mode, the initial pe0 determines only the first approximation to D. The iterative solver then finds D at the specified S/D from the brake power of the reintegrated cycle. In verification mode, D and S are specified.

Calculated bore and stroke are not nominal drawing dimensions. For preliminary adoption, D and S may be rounded upwards using increment I-177, normally 1 mm, and recalculated. Production engines need not use integer millimetres: BMW specifies D = 82 mm, S = 94.6 mm [27].

4

Intake, compression, combustion, expansion, and exhaust

Internal combustion engine calculation

A single-zone 720° cycle is integrated until a periodic state is reached. Valve flows use a compressible-nozzle model; the geometry of the centred slider-crank mechanism is exact. Two inlet and two exhaust valves use a sin² lift law without overlap.

PFI: the fresh mixture already contains fuel. GDI/diesel: air enters through the inlet, while fuel mass and its injection energy are added separately. Diesel uses an assumed ignition delay and two Wiebe phases; combustion cannot precede fuel injection.

There is no spray, NOx/soot chemistry, knock, or multizone stratification model. Boosted intake/exhaust pressures are prescribed boundary conditions, not turbocharger selection results.

The single-zone (0D) model represents gas in each cylinder as one homogeneous control volume, with one pressure and mean temperature at each instant. A single zone does not mean a single cylinder. This simplification permits rapid integration of mass and energy balances to determine p–V, work, and power; it does not resolve a flame front, spray, local temperatures, or separate fresh/burnt gas zones. The homogeneous-control-volume principle is described in [21]. This application uses its own simplified heat-capacity and heat-release laws. The dashed line on indicator diagrams represents atmospheric pressure p0 = 0.101325 MPa.

5

Performance, adopted dimensions, and characteristics

Internal combustion engine calculation

p–V work determines indicated power; mechanical losses are deducted separately. Fuel consumption follows from the cylinder charge and fuel delivery, rather than a brand-specific coefficient.

The speed series is reintegrated at every rotational speed using the same adopted control laws. It is not an optimised manufacturer's full-load characteristic. Load points are explicitly modelled; a missing EPA-map value is not replaced by zero consumption.

The separate Powertrain module accepts numerical packages with component identity, operating envelopes, and data domains. US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) packages are installed in Data/EPA; each package retains its own provenance and limitations. The characteristic calculated by this Design module remains modelled, not measured.

Kinematics, dynamics, and auxiliary systems

Internal combustion engine calculation

Pressure and geometry from the preceding chapters determine gas, inertia, resultant, connecting-rod, and crank forces without manual copying. Total torque assumes evenly spaced firing events over one active cycle: 360°/z or 720°/z.

Energy fluctuation determines the required total inertia, not the final flywheel design. Heat flow gives a preliminary coolant mass flow, not pump head or a production pump. Strength, fatigue, spatial balancing, and bearings are not fully assessed here.

The additional 0.7 assessment uses current forces for preliminary axial/Euler/Goodman, piston-pin, and torsion checks, and heat for a series hydraulic circuit. A separate explicit specification is required; this is not a complete component or fatigue-life calculation. Unknown data are marked not assessed.

Cylinder torque and power summation

For identical cylinders with evenly spaced firing: T = 720° for four-stroke or 360° for two-stroke; Δθ = T/i. Here T = 720°, i = 4, Δθ = 180°. Cyl 1…Cyl 4 identify phase positions, not a prescribed firing order of physical cylinders.

Mⱼ(θ) = M₁((θ − (j − 1)Δθ) mod T); MΣ(θ) = Σⱼ₌₁ⁱ Mⱼ(θ).

Phase shifts: 0°; 180°; 360°; 540°. Under these assumptions, the total curve repeats after Δθ and each cylinder curve after T. Uneven firing requires actual phase shifts.

ω = 2πn/60; PΣ(θ) = ωMΣ(θ); Mₑ = Pₑ/ω; Pₑ = Pᵢ − Pмех.

At n = 5 500 min⁻¹: Pᵢ = 127.4 kW; Pₑ = 110 kW; Mᵢ,сер = 221.2 N·m; Mₑ = 191 N·m. Instantaneous curves include gas forces and reciprocating-mass inertia before mechanical losses; the mean brake value is shown separately.

The full-load speed characteristic gives mean Pₑ(n) and Mₑ(n) of the complete engine at full load. This modelled characteristic uses fixed prescribed control laws; summation over crank angle θ shows pulsation at one speed n and does not replace the speed characteristic.

11

EPA maps and driving scenarios

Applications and checks

The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) publishes powertrain test-data packages and maps. In this chapter, EPA denotes the source of reference maps, not certification of this calculation.

A fuel-consumption map describes ṁf(n,M), not an indicator diagram. It does not replace the geometry, temperatures, or forces of the current engine cycle. Component identity, fuel, envelope, units, and missing values are retained [6].

Interpolation at the check point is restricted to the valid data domain. Empty and negative source cells do not become zero consumption. A map does not replace the design engine unless explicitly selected.

The current BEV vehicle and range are calculated in chapter 10. This chapter shows a separate external map for component comparison; it does not replace the calculated motor or complete vehicle.

The Bolt electric map represents motoring losses at 350 V. Inverter behaviour, a regeneration map, and verified continuous-current limits are not invented. It is used for the check point and plot; the general BEV continues to use the specified equivalent electric machine.

Strength and fatigue life: first approximation

Applications and checks

Loads come from the current cycle. The connecting rod is a bar; the pin is a simply supported beam; the shaft is a circular section in torsion. Default materials, concentration factors, and geometry are illustrative and editable.

Goodman uses the complete block's stress amplitude and mean; no benefit from compressive mean stress is credited. Euler applies only when critical stress is below the specified elastic limit. These are preliminary checks, not a spatial crankshaft analysis [12].

S–N: logarithmic interpolation between two entered reference points. One block repetition is 360° or 720° according to the selected cycle. Life is not extrapolated beyond the S–N interval; only a bound or insufficient data is stated. There is no automatically verified material fatigue curve, rainflow counting, or independent fatigue-life validation.

Simplified control strategy

Applications and checks

A first-order actuator is added to the traction source: τ dP/dt + P = Pcmd. An exact discrete solution for a constant command is used; τ and load fraction are editable educational assumptions. The transient plot is a separate check and does not modify current engine-cycle pressure.

The driving cycle uses the Powertrain limiting strategy: traction, battery charging/discharging, regeneration, P2, or series generation. Missing map points prevent reliable fuel-consumption calculation rather than disappearing from the balance. This algorithm is not ECU/BMS firmware.

The hybrid driving example separately uses a simplified power split based on demand and SOC, including current and regeneration limits. Cold starts, catalysts, knock, and manufacturer control maps are not included.

15

Comparison with measurements

Applications and checks

Paired CSV import accepts observed and predicted values with time, trip, and units. RMSE, bias, and maximum absolute error are calculated only from supplied pairs. Empty cells are excluded and counted separately.

Training and validation trips do not overlap. Until the user's measurements are supplied, the status is Not experimentally validated. The demonstration CSV checks arithmetic, not engine accuracy. The user's OBD2 data are not mixed with independent torque measurements.

No validation CSV was supplied for this calculation. Independent experimental verification has not been performed. A software test using synthetic pairs checks only metric arithmetic.
16

Conclusions, sources, and limitations

System

Mathematical tests and balances check the implementation. They are not experimental validation, test-bench calibration, or evidence of emissions compliance.

The original assignment, adopted assumptions, numerical results, and external sources remain distinct. HTML, PDF, CSV, and the native document are generated from the same state.

Conclusions concern the applicable checks for the current variant. Installed EPA reference maps are used only within their data domains. Independent testing, complete spatial strength analysis, verified fatigue life, and emissions require separate evidence.

Available output-shaft power: 110 kW. The adopted value is referenced directly from the preceding result.
